title: Error, not found, no access
description: The page-level states every app needs: ErrorState (what failed, with a retry), NotFound (a wrong URL) and Forbidden (no access), each with a link home, plus the route-file recipe (loading.tsx, error.tsx, not-found.tsx) that uses them.
when: A route or a fetch failed: ErrorState with onRetry (route error.tsx passes Next.js's reset).
An unknown URL or notFound(): NotFound. A signed-in user without the role: Forbidden.
Every Next.js route group ships loading.tsx (PageSkeleton), error.tsx (ErrorState) and not-found.tsx (NotFound).

instead.need: A list with nothing in it
A form field or action failed
instead.use: Field error text, Alert or a danger toast
PageSkeleton / Skeleton in the shape of the content

a11y: ErrorState is role="alert", so screen readers announce it; the retry is a normal button.
NotFound and Forbidden have one heading and a link home; Forbidden offers no retry.

A route-level state is the page's h1 (headingLevel={1}); inside a page keep ErrorState at h2. Below sm the state is capped at 40% of the viewport and, if its content overflows, becomes a focusable, scrollable region.
notes: Recipe: per route group put loading.tsx, error.tsx and not-found.tsx beside layout.tsx (the route-* examples), titles as h1 (`headingLevel={1}`; NotFound and Forbidden default to h1). A fully static (prerendered) site needs no loading.tsx: it would wrap every page in a Suspense boundary, so the HTML ships the page inside a hidden segment that a script swaps in. Put app/not-found.tsx at the root for URLs that match no group. A group's error.tsx does not catch errors in its own layout: add a root app/error.tsx for the root layout's children and app/global-error.tsx (it renders its own html and body) for the root layout itself.
Keep data already loaded: when a refetch fails, show ErrorState in place of the failed part only and leave the rest on screen.
Show a code or digest in `detail` for support, never the stack. Texts are Vietnamese by default and come from SemiLocaleProvider; pass title / message for product wording.
403 means signed in but not allowed (Forbidden, no retry); not signed in goes to the login page, not to Forbidden.
